items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: I tried to get Papa Celestan, but he didn't want to leave home.

ctx.x: Well, he must have been a pretty old man by this time. Huh? Charlie McCurdis was pretty old probably by this time.

Well, Charlie McCurdis was. He was much older than you. Oh, yeah. If he's living, he's a pretty old man now. I don't know if he's living. I don't know if he's living, but he's very good. He's one of the earliest. He's a very good climate player. He was. Very, very good, one of your best we had in all of the musicals, you know? So Louis Nelson was the best jazz climate player we had down there. Is that so? Yeah. Charlie McCurdis was the best musician. It's like P. and Pico. Pico was a very good musician, but he's…
Well, when you went on the boat and you started to work, did you go on a trip right away or what?

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: And this is a good friend. He was staying at my house when he come up here.

ctx.x: Is that backstage in the Paramount Theater? Yeah, that's backstage in the Paramount Theater, yeah. Yeah, with Bud Freeman. Yeah, I've seen that. Only it's a different shot, I think. The other one Louie was playing, I think.

Always wearing glasses. This is a little bit of sketchy. Now, this is when Papa Sutterstatt come up here to visit the player of the date up here, this big chief trombone player, this big Indian chief. Who was that? That was at the Metro Bowl. Oh, in New York. New York, see? Oh, I didn't remember. See, Papa Sutterstatt, see? And this is a good friend. He was staying at my house when he come up here. Uh-huh. See? And I went down to this big chief, big Indian trombone player.
Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. He was the last I heard him, uh...
